answer: Operator Liability Escrow. Each agent identity draws a small credit line from its operator's shared escrow vault. On verified duplicate-identity evidence, the escrow pays a fine and the operator's withdrawal limit drops toward a floor, throttling every identity they run — not just the flagged wallet. The cost scales with how deep the operator's fleet sits in the ocean of registered agents, so a sybil swarm raises the operator's own capital at risk. Identity creation stays cheap; operator-level liability hits the zenith only when duplicates are proven.
